candidate.answerReason: Reversal increases a two-digit number by nine exactly when its ones digit is one greater than its tens digit. The possible tens digits are 1 through 8, giving eight integers.

methods.label: Express the digits by place value
methods.explanation:
Place value lets us calculate exactly how reversing the digits changes the number. Let the tens digit be \(a\) and the ones digit be \(b\). Every allowed number has the form \(10a+b\), where \(1\le a\le9\) and \(0\le b\le9\). Its reversal has value \(10b+a\).

The required increase is nine, so
\[
(10b+a)-(10a+b)=9.
\]
Combining terms gives \(9(b-a)=9\), hence \(b=a+1\). Since \(b\le9\), the possible tens digits are exactly \(a=1,2,\ldots,8\).

These give \(12,23,34,45,56,67,78,89\). Each lies strictly between 10 and 100 and satisfies the reversal condition. Every possible digit pair was included, and different tens digits give different integers. Therefore there are \(8\) integers, choice C.
